title: The Frequency of Salt
social_caption: Elias lived for the silence of the 2026 winter, but the static on frequency 104.2 had started to breathe. The Old Needle lighthouse sat three hundred feet below the Atlantic, yet every night, the radio hissed: the light still holds. His late father always warned that the sea doesn't just drown men; it recruits them. Tonight, the voice on the copper speakers lost its static, becoming Elias’s own voice reporting for duty. He felt the familiar weight of the deep-trench pressure crushing his ribs while he sat in his dry kitchen. As he looked at his reflection, his eyes had turned to cold, rotating glass. The light still holds, he whispered, as the salt-water finally filled his lungs and the cottage dissolved into the dark, hungry waves.
